issues.issue: Page 9 does not print the split. It was derived from p5 (governmental charges 3,361 + keno 3,172 + interest 5,894 + contributions 2,425 + sale of property 4,425 + misc 540 = 19,817) and p7 (business-type sales 87,489 + interest 48 = 87,537). The arithmetic is exact (19,817 + 87,537 = 107,354), and the split keeps fund types apart, but under the strict rule a split must be printed for that line. It is marked review and computed. Needs human confirmation.
Business-type half of the same derived split (see detail[4]); arithmetic correct.

Governmental transfers in are only 82,775 (Street Fund, p5). The other 80,000 equals the business-type net transfers in (143,000 in - 63,000 out, p7), so part of this line belongs to business-type funds. Tagging the whole line governmental is questionable.
All 57,138 is in the Street Fund (p5), and the Statement of Activities (p3) calls it 'State allocation'. It is most likely highway allocation; this is a judgment call with no review flag.

The proprietary statements are modified cash basis, and the rule says measure = 'cash' on a cash basis. Beginning net position 91,007 includes 10,744 of certificates of deposit, so the cash measure would begin at 80,263. Net position is used and reconciles (91,007 + 87,537 - 241,204 + 80,000 = 17,340). This is a defensible assumption the extractor made; notes explain it.
